subject: How to add CSS/JavaScript to interactive Rmarkdown doc running shiny engine?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: How to add CSS/JavaScript to interactive Rmarkdown doc running shiny engine?
parts:
Here is a simple Shiny app that produces red text because of included CSS

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    tags$head(tags$style("#foo { color: red; }")),
    div(id = "foo", "bar")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
  }
)


I'm wondering how I can replicate this in an rmarkdown document that runs Shiny, such as this

---
runtime: shiny
---

```{r, echo = F}
library(shiny)

fluidPage(
  tags$head(tags$style("#foo { color: red; }")),
  div(id = "foo", "bar")
) 
```


This code produces the text "bar" but it doesn't appear in red because the CSS doesn't get included.
I don't have much experience with interactive docs that include shiny components so I'm not sure if my example if even correct.

Ah yes, that works, so simple.  Thanks Joe

Follow-up question: if I have a function that adds a script to a shiny app, e.g.

addscript <- function(){ tags$head(includeScript("foo.js")) }

And this function works well for proper shiny apps when called from the UI, do you know what would be a good way to allow this function to be used in rmarkdown docs as well?  Would I have to somehow determine if I'm currently inside an rmarkdown or not, and based on that include or omit the tags$head?  That doesn't sound too clean, hopefully someone has a better idea
